reasoning.Student A:
The mechanism specifies that which schools are in my "Obtainable Schools" set is fixed given others' rankings and priorities and cannot be changed by how I rank the schools. My submitted ranking only selects which school I receive from that fixed set — I get the highest-ranked school among the obtainable ones.

Because of that, there is no strategic advantage to misrepresenting preferences: the best outcome I can ensure is to put my true most-preferred school at the top so that, if it is obtainable, I receive it. My priorities (w:1, y:1, x:2, z:2) and the fact other applicants favor y > x > w > z may affect which schools are in the obtainable set, but they do not change the dominance of ranking truthfully. Therefore I should submit my true preference order w > x > y > z so I obtain the most-preferred school available to me.
reasoning.Student B:
Key property: my ranking cannot change which schools are in my Obtainable Schools; it only selects the highest-ranked school within that fixed set. Therefore the only sensible strategy is to rank schools in true preference order so that, whatever the obtainable set is, I receive the most-preferred school from that set.

My true preference is x > w > y > z. Additional observations that support this truthful ranking:
- I have top priority (1) at x and z, and second priority (2) at w and y. That makes x particularly attractive and likely to be obtainable compared with schools where many applicants prefer y first.
- Many other applicants prefer y > x > w > z, so competition at y may be higher; but since my ranking cannot alter which schools I could get, listing y ahead of w would only matter if y were obtainable and I preferred it over w. I do not prefer y over w, so I rank w above y.
- Thus, to guarantee I get the best school available to me, I should submit my true order x > w > y > z.

In short: because the mechanism gives me the highest-ranked school among a fixed obtainable set, report sincere preferences so I get the best outcome within that set.

The only way to improve my outcome is to ensure that, among the obtainable schools, the one I most prefer is ranked highest on my list.
